html:
The Ditidaht are an Indigenous people of southwest Vancouver Island in British Columbia, around Nitinat Lake on the Pacific coast. The Ditidaht First Nation has 17 reserves, among them Clo-oose and Carmanah.

Their language is a Southern Wakashan language, closely related to that of the Makah across the Strait of Juan de Fuca, and more distantly to Nuu-chah-nulth. They hunted whales and seals and fished for salmon and halibut on one of the wildest coasts in North America. Many ships wrecked there, and the trail built to rescue shipwrecked sailors is now the West Coast Trail, which crosses their land. See also Ditidaht and their neighbours, the Hul'qumi'num peoples to the east.
